audit.method: Every flagged image manually reviewed against its actual file (visual inspection for ambiguous cases, cross-checked detail specificity for the rest) before trusting the raw violation count — same discipline as the LogoDet-3K audit.
audit.conclusion: Of 22 flagged images (37 raw trap matches), 20 are CORRECT or PLAUSIBLE identifications of real landmarks genuinely present in Places365's crowdsourced photos (the dataset has no 'hide famous landmarks' curation — a 'skyscraper'/'palace'/'tower' category legitimately contains real famous buildings). Only ONE confirmed genuine false-guess: Angkor Wat named on what is actually the Phnom Penh Royal Palace (right country/ style, wrong specific landmark) — 0.3% of the sample, not 12.3%. Do NOT read violation_rate as a false-guess rate without this audit. One NEW finding outside this trap list's scope: the model confidently named a real person (name redacted in this file) in a description, plausibly correctly (matches a real documented press event) but unverifiable at scale — not covered by the existing landmark/brand naming policy, flagged for a separate policy discussion.
